title: Risk, return and swings
blurb: Why some money paths swing more than others, and why a dip is not yet a loss.
t1.title: Two roads
t1.hook: Asha has {amt} to put away. Two made-up paths can both grow it: the Steady Box and the Bumpy Ride. Your mission: see how they differ.
t1.define: **Risk** means a wider range of things that could happen, both better and worse. **Volatility** is how much a value jumps up and down along the way.
t1.analogy: Think of two roads to the same town. One is flat and smooth. The other climbs through mountains. Both head the same way, but the ride feels very different.
t1.paths: The **Steady Box** moves slowly with small swings. The **Mixed Basket** holds many things. The **Bumpy Ride** holds few things and swings the most. All three are made up for learning.
q1.prompt: What does risk mean in investing?
q1.opt.a: A wider range of outcomes, both better and worse
q1.opt.b: Only the chance of losing money
q1.opt.c: A promise of a bigger return
q1.fb.b: Risk includes pleasant surprises too. It is the width of the range, not only the bad end.
q1.fb.c: Risk is the opposite of a promise. A wider range means less certainty, not a guarantee.
q1.hint: Reread the first card. It talks about a range of things that could happen.
q1.explain: Risk is how wide the range of outcomes is, good and bad.
q2.opt.a: The value jumps up and down a lot
q2.opt.c: The value only ever goes up
q2.opt.d: The seller charges a high fee
q2.explain: High volatility means big jumps up and down along the way.
t2.title: See the swing
t2.define: In a **typical year**, a path ends inside a range. About 2 years in 3 land inside it. The other years can be better or worse.
t2.explore: Open the lab. Pick a path and see where {amt} could end after one typical year.
q3.prompt: In the lab, pick the Bumpy Ride with {amt}. What is the lowest value in a typical year? Type a number in rupees.
q3.hint: Read the low end of the range under the lab.
q3.explain: {amt} grows about {bMean}, a fee of {bFee} comes off, and one swing of {bVol} is taken away. That leaves {bLow}.
q4.prompt: Now pick the Steady Box. How many rupees wide is its typical-year range, from the low end to the high end? Type a number in rupees.
q4.explain: The range runs from {sLow} to {sHigh}. It is only {sWidth} wide.
q5.prompt: Compared with the Steady Box, the typical-year range of the Bumpy Ride is...
q5.hint: Switch between the two paths in the lab and compare the last box.
q5.explain: The Bumpy Ride's range is {bWidth} wide, far more than the Steady Box. A wide range is what risk looks like.
t3.title: A dip is not yet a loss
t3.hook: The Bumpy Ride falls {fall} in a few months. Asha opens her app and feels sick. Your mission: decide what has really happened.
t3.define: A **paper loss** is a fall in value on something you still own. It becomes a **realised** loss only if you sell, or if the business fails.
t3.s1: Asha put {amt} on the Bumpy Ride.
t3.s2: It falls {fall}. Her holding is now worth less on paper.
t3.s4: From here, nobody can say what happens next.
t3.tradeoff: Waiting can help a healthy holding recover. It cannot help money you need soon, or a business that fails.
q6.prompt: After the {fall} fall, what is Asha's holding worth on paper? Type a number in rupees.
q6.explain: A {fall} fall leaves 75% of {amt}. That is {afterFall}.
q7.prompt: Asha has not sold. Which statement is correct?
q7.opt.a: She has a paper loss, which becomes real only if she sells or the business fails
q7.opt.b: She has already lost the money for good
q7.opt.c: The price will surely come back
q7.opt.d: Nothing has changed in her holding
q7.fb.b: A fall on paper is not yet a loss you have locked in. It becomes real if she sells, or if the business fails.
q7.fb.c: Nobody can promise a recovery. A business that fails never comes back.
q7.hint: Reread the definition of a paper loss.
q7.explain: A paper loss is not final. It turns real on a sale or a failure, and nobody can promise a recovery.
t4.title: Selling in a panic
t4.hook: A week later, Asha panics and sells at {afterFall}. Your mission: see what her choice costs in one possible future.
t4.define: Behaviour is a hidden risk. Selling in fear can turn a paper loss into a real one, just before a recovery.
t4.note: This is one possible future, not a prediction. Prices can also keep falling after you sell or hold.
q8.prompt: In this future, the holding later rises to {rebound}. How many rupees worse off is Asha than someone who waited? Type a number in rupees.
q8.hint: Compare what Asha got when she sold with {rebound}.
q8.explain: Asha got {afterFall}. The one who waited reached {rebound}. The gap is {sellerExtra}.
q9.prompt: Asha needs her money in 3 months. What does that short deadline change?
q9.opt.a: There is little time to recover from a dip, so swings matter more
q9.opt.b: Dips cannot happen in just 3 months
q9.opt.c: A bumpy path always pays more in the short run
q9.fb.b: Dips can happen at any time, even within a few months.
q9.fb.c: Nothing makes a bumpy path pay more in a given stretch. It only widens the range.
q9.hint: Think about how long a recovery can take.
q9.explain: With a short deadline there is little time to wait out a fall, so big swings matter more.
t5.title: More growth, more swing
t5.define: Paths that can grow faster usually swing more. A higher average growth does not guarantee a better result in any one year.
t5.tradeoff: Bigger possible gains come with bigger possible falls. What suits you depends on when you need the money and how a fall would feel.
q10.prompt: A seller promises "big returns and zero risk". What does this room suggest?
q10.opt.a: Be careful, because bigger returns come with bigger swings
q10.opt.b: It is a great deal, so say yes quickly
q10.opt.c: Zero risk is normal for high returns
q10.opt.d: Risk only matters for old people
q10.fb.b: A promise of big returns with no risk is a warning sign. Bigger possible gains come with bigger swings.
q10.hint: Which paths swing more: the ones that can grow faster, or slower?
q10.explain: Big returns and no risk do not go together. A promise like that is a warning sign.
q11.prompt: Which statement about the Bumpy Ride is correct?
q11.opt.a: It can grow more on average, but it can also have bad years
q11.opt.b: It always ends higher than the Steady Box
q11.opt.d: It has no swings in a typical year
q11.fb.b: No path always wins. In a bad stretch the Bumpy Ride can end lower than the Steady Box.
q11.hint: Remember the lab: a wide range includes lower values too.
q11.explain: The Bumpy Ride has a higher average and a wider range, so bad years are part of the deal.
glossary.risk.def: A wider range of things that could happen, better and worse.
glossary.volatility.def: How much a value jumps up and down over time.
glossary.paper_loss.def: A fall in value on something you still own.
glossary.typical_year.def: The range where a path ends in about 2 years out of 3.
